hypotheses.justification: hqN is an instance-implicit variable whose type mentions only q and N, which are already arguments, so the theorem takes it automatically. The statement never uses it. `PlaceSpecialization.fstDiv` is defined in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_GlueData.lean as `D.filter P.IsStrictFst`. That file has no `Fact (¬ q ∣ N)` variable, and neither does `PlaceSpecialization` (which needs only `Fact q.Prime`, `NeZero N` and `CharP k q`). `Divisor (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (modularFunctionFieldBar (N*q))` also elaborates in that file without it. So the statement `P.fstDiv (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, P.fstDiv (f i)` is the same without hqN, and it is true: `fstDiv` is `Finsupp.filter`, which is additive. The only way the proof touches hqN is the call to the local `fstDiv_add`, which itself takes hqN from the same `variable` line. Replace that call with `Finsupp.filter_add` (the lemma `fstDiv_add` uses). The `empty` case already uses `Finsupp.filter_zero` and needs no hqN. Use `omit hqN in` before the theorem.
